articleTitle: Considerations in the selection and supervision of VLSI design projects
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: VLSI design encompasses a wide range of skills including, at one extreme the specification of a design using a hardware description language such as VHDL and at the other extreme, polygon level layout of high performance analogue circuits. It is not possible to address the entire range in a single project so a sub-range must be chosen. This presentation describes the approach to address this subject, taken at the University of Kent.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VLSI design and implementation of a simple 4*4 Hopfield neural network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: Several difficulties can arise when scaling up the size of a neural network; one is that the computational time can become prohibitive. One approach to scaling is to build accelerated hardware, such as customised VLSI circuits. Integrated circuits can provide some acceleration to the neural network computations and would, in addition, implement the network in an extremely compact form. This paper describes the first stage of implementation of a simple Hopfield neural network in VLSI, and was carried out as a final year undergraduate student design project at Liverpool University.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VLSI design within an integrated engineering course
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: An important and increasing number of students remain either broad based across all disciplines, or straddle a selection of disciplines. Some years ago these students would have been typified by course choices which included mechanical and electrical, or electrical and electronic subjects. A recent development is an increase in those who wish to pursue mechanical and electronic engineering, the so called 'mechatronics' subjects. Subdividing even further, interest is being shown in plastics processing and electronics (with the VLSI option). The latter students have indicated that their intended occupation is within the plastics industry. It is within such an environment that the teaching of VLSI design will be described. A course in VLSI was added to the list of optional courses available to final year students in 1986, and has been running since then. Total numbers of students taking the course have been in the range 30 to 40 each year.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New directions in VLSI teaching in London University
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: The London University VLSI Consortium was established in 1982 so that the Electronic Engineering and Computer Science Departments of London University could co-operate to obtain design tools and fabrication facilities for integrated circuit design teaching. At the time of the Eurochip initiative there were therefore established VLSI design courses at the five major sites of London University King's College, Imperial College, Queen Mary and Westfield College, Royal Holloway and Bedford New College and University College. These courses all included fabrication of custom VLSI circuits, using full-custom design tools or SOLO 1400. Eurochip was therefore seen as an opportunity to improve the quality of the teaching that had already been established, and in particular to strengthen teaching areas considered to be of industrial importance but where the existing academic staff considered that they had limited expertise. The two areas that it was believed would benefit most from the introduction of new material were chip architectures (including the problems of managing complexity) and analogue design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An MSc. gate array design exercise
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: Through a gate array design exercise students on a one-year MSc. Electronics Course are given practical experience in using CAD tools in the field of semi-custom integrated circuit design. The resulting circuits, which are fabricated commercially, can be seen operating in demonstration projects. Various software packages have been used over a number of years.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using advanced CAD tools to teach basic VLSI skills
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: This paper proposes using a variety of high level design tools, obtained through the Eurochip scheme, to enable students to perform comparative studies on a range of design problems. This approach not only highlights the advantages and disadvantages of different methodologies but also helps to develop an understanding of the low level circuit techniques being used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a VLSI-based artificial neural network system by a student group
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: Describes the subject of a particular group of projects carried out by undergraduate, MSc and PhD students, over the past three years. The projects relate to the analysis, design, development and construction of a VLSI-based artificial neural network (ANN) system. The projects have been carefully specified so that they complement each other without significant overlap. In general, the projects fall into one of three categories: applications development (e.g. speech recognition, image recognition, robot control), systems analysis (e.g. hardware configuration requirements for optimum system performance), and hardware design and development (e.g. design of a VLSI IC, design of a demonstrator system for the IC, design of input/output instrumentation such as CCD imagers or robot motion control components). As well as providing for a range of skill/ability levels from construction to open ended research, the projects enable students to concentrate on specific subject areas ranging from software engineering (applications) through hardware/software (systems analysis) to hardware design at IC, PCB and system levels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EUROCHIP postgraduate and undergraduate projects in the electronic and electrical engineering department of University College London
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: Describes approaches to education as manifested in various ASIC designs performed in the electronic and electrical engineering department at UCL under the Eurochip initiative. The work described spans requirements for both course-work and project-work in undergraduate courses, MSc courses and advanced work for PhD programmes. Finally, the authors will attempt to draw some conclusions about an optimal approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: At the Polytechnic of Central London (PCL), undergraduate level MOS VLSI design is taught through a 3-year BEng course of unusual structure, style and pacing. In this paper, an outline of the course is presented together with experiences relating to its delivery and associated full-custom and digital semi-custom student project work.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and test of VLSI circuits: a Eurochip perspective
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: Provides a Eurochip perspective on the design and test of VLSI circuits. It focuses on: the need to link the design of digital or analogue devices to a degree of self test; the importance of routes to silicon through Eurochip; and the need for adequate fault simulation software to amalgamate self-test on a chip.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VLSI design teaching in a computer science department
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: VLSI technology has had a profound influence on the development of computing systems over the past decade. The Eurochip project was therefore welcomed by the computer science department at Manchester University as an opportunity to develop new courses in VLSI design which would give students the opportunity to become involved in the design of systems on silicon. The teaching of VLSI design within the department, aimed at three different groups of students, is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mixed signal ASIC design with SOLO 1400
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Eurochip Project - VLSI Design in Higher Education
abstract: With SOLO 1400 a mixed signal ASIC of moderate complexity can be tackled with a reasonably high degree of confidence in a successful outcome. The objective set for each design group was to replace the control electronics of a commercially available radio controlled model car. This choice was based on the assumption that the task would have a strong appeal that would not prove too difficult conceptually for undergraduates at an early stage in their course while at the same time requiring both digital and analogue subsystems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
